subject: Insurance
title: Hole-in-One Insurance
description: A micro-lesson that makes Hole-in-One Insurance usable.

hook.text: Golf tournaments offer car prizes for a hole-in-one. The sponsor doesn't pay—an insurer does.

buildup.text: A $50,000 car prize costs the sponsor only $200-500 in premiums. The insurer bets nobody will make the shot.

discovery.text: The odds of a hole-in-one for an amateur are about 12,500 to 1. For a pro, about 2,500 to 1.

twist.text: Some tournaments have seen multiple holes-in-one at the same event.

climax.text: Prize indemnity insurance is pure probability business. Insurers aren't insuring risk—they're betting on statistics.

punchline.text: $200 premium, $50,000 car prize. Insurers bet you'll miss.

quiz.question: What are the approximate odds of an amateur making a hole-in-one?
